newsitem.title: EGYPT: Ross says common ground needed for Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Ross says common ground needed for Hebron talks.

text.p: A U.S. envoy to the Middle East said on Saturday the Israeli and Palestinian sides had "basically" resolved the issue of Israel's withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron but that other problems remained.
Middle East peace mediator Dennis Ross said he told Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak during their meeting earlier in the day that "we basically have resolved the Hebron issue".
"We achieved a great deal of progress...but we have not overcome all the differences yet," Ross told reporters.
"We made a lot of progress on the Hebron issues and we still have gaps on some of the non-Hebron issues," he said.

Ross on Saturday met with a team led by chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa as part of efforts to push forward faltering peace negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.

"What I was doing is an extension of what I have been doing which is, as we look at some of these non-Hebron issues, is there a way for us to find sufficient common ground on them," Ross said about his meeting at the foreign ministry.
"We are still working on these issues. We don't have agreement yet," Ross said.

Palestinian-Israeli talks on an Israeli pullout from 80 percent of Hebron have been deadlocked over Palestinians' insistence that Israel adhere to a 1995 interim peace deal that requires withdrawal from various other parts of the West Bank by September 1997.
Asked whether a "common ground" could be reached on Saturday or Sunday, Erekat said: "I do not think that we should confine ourselves to a timeframe."
The Palestinian negotiator said this depended on the willingness of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to implement the agreements already signed.

"I think the minute, the second, Mr. Netanyahu makes up his mind and gives his negotiator the green light to stick to the agreement signed in Washington... I think we will move to implement the outstanding commitments in the agreement."
"The main sticking point is not something easy. It is the nucleus of the interim agreement. It is the further redeployments," said Erekat.
Ross had met earlier in the day at a Cairo palace with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, who also held separate talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Arafat, who later returned to Gaza, pays regular visits to Egypt to brief Mubarak on developments in the peace talks.
